vulnerabilities.description: CVE-2022-0839 is an XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability in Liquibase Core versions prior to 4.8.0 via the SAXParser. An attacker could exploit this to read arbitrary files or perform server-side request forgery (SSRF) through crafted XML changelog files.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure 4.8.0+ includes the fix. All current Liquibase Secure distributions are built from source with the patched SAXParser configuration.
vulnerabilities.workaround: If using Liquibase < 4.8.0, disable XML changelog parsing or upgrade to 4.8.0+. Alternatively, ensure all changelog files come from trusted sources only.

ratings.justification: Code path containing the vulnerability is not present in Liquibase Secure builds. NVD score reflects theoretical maximum; contextual score reflects actual exploitability.

analysis.detail: XXE vulnerability fixed in Liquibase 4.8.0. Our liquibase-core is built from source with the fix included. Scanner incorrectly matches the non-semantic version format (master-<sha>).
False CPE match. liquibase-commercial-mongodb is a Liquibase extension, not MongoDB server. The vulnerability applies to MongoDB server only.

This CVE requires setuptools to process package inputs; no package installation or processing occurs at runtime.

vulnerabilities.description: Apache OpenNLP AbstractModelReader allocates unbounded memory when reading model files, allowing a malicious or malformed model file to cause an out-of-memory denial of service.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure. OpenNLP models are pre-bundled trusted artifacts; no attacker-controlled model loading occurs.

ratings.justification: Liquibase does not load model files from untrusted sources. Pre-bundled trusted models are used; AbstractModelReader is not directly invoked by Liquibase code.

analysis.detail: Apache OpenNLP AbstractModelReader OOM denial-of-service vulnerability via unbounded memory allocation during model loading. Exploitation requires loading an attacker-controlled or malformed model file. Liquibase Secure bundles pre-packaged, trusted OpenNLP model files at build time; no model files are loaded from external or user-controlled sources at runtime. AbstractModelReader is not imported or called directly in Liquibase code.

vulnerabilities.description: The Dial and LookupPort functions panic on Windows when provided with an input containing a NUL (0).
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure Docker images. The vulnerable behavior requires a Windows runtime environment, while the assessed image is Linux-based.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires Windows, but the assessed Docker image uses a Linux base image.

vulnerabilities.description: When using LookupCNAME with the cgo DNS resolver, a very long CNAME response can trigger a double-free of C memory and a crash.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. lpm does not call LookupCNAME and the cgo DNS resolver is not active on Linux.

ratings.justification: lpm never calls LookupCNAME. Hostname resolution for HTTP downloads uses LookupIPAddr. The cgo DNS resolver is not the default on Linux.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib LookupCNAME double-free in the cgo DNS resolver when processing a very long CNAME response. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it downloads Liquibase extension driver JARs from GitHub release assets via HTTP. lpm never calls LookupCNAME — standard HTTP hostname resolution uses LookupIPAddr/LookupHost, not the CNAME-specific API. Additionally, the vulnerability requires the cgo DNS resolver, which is not the default on Linux; the pure-Go DNS resolver is active in the eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble container.

vulnerabilities.description: When processing HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames, transport will enter an infinite loop of writing CONTINUATION frames if it receives a SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. lpm only connects to trusted GitHub release servers.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib HTTP/2 transport infinite loop when a server sends SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it makes HTTP/2 connections to GitHub release servers to download Liquibase extension driver JARs. Exploitation requires a server to send the malformed SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE=0 frame. lpm only connects to trusted GitHub release CDN endpoints (URLs and checksums fixed in docker/Dockerfile:35-55); no attacker- controlled server endpoint exists in lpm's execution path.

Improper Authorization vulnerability when multiple method constraints define an HTTP method for the same extension in Apache Tomcat.
This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109.

vulnerabilities.description: (*x509.Certificate).VerifyHostname previously called matchHostnames in a loop over all DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. This caused strings.Split(host, ".") to execute repeatedly on the same input hostname. With a large DNS SAN list, verification costs scaled quadratically based on the number of SAN entries multiplied by the hostname's label count. Because x509.Verify validates hostnames before building the certificate chain, this overhead occurred even for untrusted certificates.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for default Liquibase Secure Docker usage. The vulnerable Go TLS hostname verification path is only reachable when the optional lpm helper is explicitly invoked, and current Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.5 built with fixed Go 1.25.11.

ratings.justification: Liquibase Secure Docker does not run the optional lpm helper unless INSTALL_MYSQL is explicitly configured or a user directly invokes lpm; the default runtime executes the Java Liquibase CLI instead. Current Docker builds also install an lpm release built with a fixed Go toolchain.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib crypto/x509 VerifyHostname quadratic complexity vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.11 and 1.26.4. vulnerabilities.description: ReverseProxy can forward queries containing parameters not visible to Rewrite functions. When used with a Rewrite function, or a Director function which parses query parameters, ReverseProxy sanitizes the forwarded request to remove query parameters which are not parsed by url.ParseQuery. ReverseProxy does not take ParseQuery's limit on the total number of query parameters (controlled by GODEBUG=urlmaxqueryparams=N) into account. This can permit ReverseProxy to forward a request containing a query parameter that is not visible to the Rewrite function. For example, the query "a1=x&a2=x&...&a10000=x&hidden=y" can forward the parameter "hidden=y" while hiding it from the proxy's Rewrite function.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. Prior to versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final, Netty's `DnsResolveContext` insufficiently validates the bailiwick of NS records, enabling DNS Cache Poisoning. An attacker controlling an authoritative name server for a subdomain can poison the cache for parent domains (like `.co.uk`). In `io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsResolveContext.AuthoritativeNameServerList#add` method accepts any NS record from the AUTHORITY section as long as the record's name is a suffix of the questionName. Subsequently, the `handleWithAdditional` method caches the associated A records from the ADDITIONAL section directly into the `authoritativeDnsServerCache` under the parent domain's key. This bypasses standard bailiwick rules, where a server authoritative for a subdomain should not be trusted to provide authoritative records for its parent. The poisoned cache is then used for all future resolutions under the parent domain's key. Versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final patch the issue.

vulnerabilities.description:
Issue summary: A specially crafted PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed message could trigger a use-after-free during PKCS#7 signature verification.
Impact summary: A use-after-free may result in process crashes, heap corruption, or potentially remote code execution.
When processing a PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed message, if the SignedData digestAlgorithms field is present as an empty ASN.1 SET, OpenSSL may incorrectly free a caller-owned BIO during PKCS7_verify(). A subsequent use of the BIO by the calling application results in a use-after-free condition.
In the common case this occurs when the application later calls BIO_free() on the BIO originally passed to PKCS7_verify(). Depending on allocator behavior and application-specific BIO usage patterns, this may result in a crash or other memory corruption. In some application contexts this may potentially be exploitable for remote code execution.
Applications that process PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed messages using OpenSSL PKCS#7 APIs may be affected. Applications using the CMS APIs for this processing are not affected.
The FIPS modules in 4.0, 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, and 3.0 are not affected by this issue, as the affected code is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not process PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed messages through OpenSSL PKCS#7 APIs.

ratings.justification: Liquibase Secure does not invoke OpenSSL PKCS#7/S/MIME verification APIs or runtime OpenSSL tooling, so the vulnerable code path is not reachable from the application.

analysis.detail: OpenSSL PKCS#7/S/MIME signature verification use-after-free. The scanner reported Ubuntu Jammy libssl3 packages below fixed package 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.25, but this assessment does not rely on a version-fixed claim because the OS package version is inherited from the base image rather than pinned in repository source. Liquibase Secure inherits OS packages from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2), and the runtime entrypoint dispatches to user-supplied commands or /liquibase/liquibase rather than OpenSSL PKCS#7 tooling (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8, docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:109, docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119, docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:121). The vulnerable path is not reachable: a focused grep for PKCS7_verify, PKCS7_, PKCS7, PKCS#7, S/MIME, SMIME, smime, BIO_free, and digestAlgorithms across repository sources returned zero hits.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. From 2.10.0 until 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4, jackson-databind's PolymorphicTypeValidator (PTV) is the primary safety mechanism guarding polymorphic deserialization. When polymorphic typing is enabled and a type identifier contains generic parameters (i.e. the type ID string contains <), DatabindContext._resolveAndValidateGeneric() validates only the raw container class name (the substring before <) against the configured PTV. If the container type is approved, the method parses the full canonical type string via TypeFactory.constructFromCanonical() and returns the fully parameterized type without ever validating the nested type arguments against the PTV. The nested type arguments are then resolved, instantiated, and populated as beans during deserialization. An attacker who controls the type ID can therefore place a denied class as a generic type parameter of an allowed container — for example java.util.ArrayList<com.evil.Gadget> when only java.util.ArrayList is allow-listed. The container passes the PTV check; com.evil.Gadget is loaded via Class.forName(name, true, loader), instantiated, and its properties are set from attacker-controlled JSON. This completely bypasses an explicitly configured PTV allow-list. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. vulnerabilities.description: On Unix systems, opening a file in an os.Root improperly follows symlinks to locations outside of the Root when the final path component of the path is a symbolic link and the path ends in /. For example, root.Open("symlink/") will open "symlink" even when "symlink" is a symbolic link pointing outside of the root.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The lpm helper bundled with Liquibase Secure Docker images does not call the os.Root API, and lpm is only invoked when INSTALL_MYSQL is explicitly configured — the default runtime path never executes it.

ratings.justification: liquibase-package-manager does not import or call the os.Root / OpenRoot APIs anywhere in its source, so the vulnerable symlink resolution path is unreachable regardless of the underlying Go stdlib version. lpm is also only invoked from the Docker entrypoint when INSTALL_MYSQL is explicitly configured.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib os.Root symlink-following vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.12, 1.26.5, and 1.27.0-rc.2. The scanner reported affected Go stdlib version v1.26.4 in the lpm helper bundled in published Liquibase Secure Docker images (docker/Dockerfile:35, docker/Dockerfile:49) — confirmed by extracting the released liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 binary and running `go version` on it, which reports go1.26.4, matching the scanner's reported installed version exactly. The vulnerable API, os.Root (and OpenRoot), is a defensive filesystem-sandboxing API added in Go 1.24; a source-level grep of the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 repository for os.Root, OpenRoot, and .Root( returned zero hits, so lpm does not use the vulnerable API at all. Defense in depth: the Secure Docker entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is explicitly configured (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4); the default runtime path executes the Java Liquibase CLI directly and never calls lpm (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119-121).

vulnerabilities.description: Jackson Core's async parser can accumulate excessively long digit sequences (~20,000x amplification of the intended maxNumberLength limit) when input is fed in small chunks without a terminator, weakening DoS protection for applications that rely on maxNumberLength.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run a reactive/async network-facing service that parses untrusted JSON with this parser. Track upstream fix (2.18.8 / 2.21.4 / 2.22.1) for the next dependency refresh.

ratings.justification: Client-side use only, against trusted cloud-provider endpoints; no attacker-controlled JSON is parsed via the vulnerable non-blocking parser API.

analysis.detail: Incomplete fix for a prior number-length constraint bypass: Jackson's async/non-blocking parser (NonBlockingJsonParser / ByteArrayFeeder) silently buffers digit characters up to maxStringLength instead of enforcing maxNumberLength when input arrives in small chunks without a terminator byte. Found in jackson-core 2.22.0 bundled into liquibase-aws-extension.jar and liquibase-azure.jar. Both extensions are outbound clients that call AWS/Azure APIs and parse the responses those services return over TLS; neither extension's own code invokes Jackson's non-blocking parser API, and neither exposes a network-facing endpoint that accepts attacker-controlled JSON. Exploiting this would require an attacker already able to forge or MITM AWS/Azure API responses, at which point far more direct attacks are already available.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. analysis.detail: Netty SPDY SETTINGS decoder unbounded map amplification, fixed in 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final. A focused grep for SpdySettingsFrame, SpdyFrameCodec, and io.netty.handler.codec.spdy across Java and XML sources returned zero hits, and Liquibase never runs a SPDY server or client.

PostgreSQL JDBC driver channel binding bypass. The vulnerability only triggers when the JDBC connection property channelBinding is explicitly set to "require" (default is "prefer"). Liquibase does not configure channelBinding=require in any default configuration. The vulnerable enforcement code path in ConnectionFactoryImpl.doAuthentication() is not reachable under Liquibase's default configuration.

vulnerabilities.description: channelBinding=require connections can be silently downgraded from SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS with channel binding to plain SCRAM-SHA-256 without it. An attacker able to intercept the TLS connection could exploit this by presenting certificates with unsupported signature algorithms, causing the authentication mechanism to lose its man-in-the-middle protection.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for the default configuration, since Liquibase does not set channelBinding itself. Deployments that explicitly set channelBinding=require in their own JDBC URL should use a Liquibase Secure build on pgjdbc 42.7.12 or later (current source already pins 42.7.13); already-published images built before that bump remain exposed for that specific configuration until upgraded.

ratings.justification: Liquibase's default configuration never sets channelBinding=require (or any channelBinding value), so the default deployment has no channel-binding guarantee for this CVE to downgrade. Deployments that explicitly configure channelBinding=require in their own JDBC URL remain exposed until the resolved pgjdbc version is 42.7.12+. NVD also rates this 8.2/HIGH under CVSSv4 — noted here since the CVSSv3.1 base score alone understates why internal scanners may surface it as high severity.

analysis.detail: pgjdbc channel-binding downgrade: connections configured with channelBinding=require can be silently downgraded from SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS (with channel binding) to plain SCRAM-SHA-256 (without it) when the server presents a certificate with an unsupported signature algorithm, defeating the MITM protection channelBinding=require is meant to provide. Fixed in pgjdbc 42.7.12. channelBinding is a pgjdbc JDBC URL/connection property; a repo-wide grep (`grep -rn "channelBinding" --include="*.java" --include="*.properties" --include="*.yml" .`) confirms Liquibase's own code never sets it. However, the --url argument is a raw user-supplied JDBC URL passed straight through with no property filtering (DbUrlConnectionCommandStep.java:107-120: `url = commandScope.getArgumentValue(URL_ARG)` flows unmodified into createDatabaseObject()), so a deployment where the user has appended channelBinding=require to their own connection URL — a deliberate, security-conscious choice some users make — remains exposed to this downgrade until the resolved pgjdbc version is 42.7.12+. This is therefore not reachable in Liquibase's *default* configuration, but is reachable if a user opts into channelBinding=require. Independently, the current source already pins the fix by default: pom.xml:62 sets postgresql.version to 42.7.13, and dist/pom.xml:123 consumes that managed version — the scanner reported 42.7.11 on the published 5.2.0 image (built before this version bump).

This CVE requires setuptools to process URLs via download/install functions; those functions are never called at runtime.

Spring Framework annotation resolution bypass in generic type hierarchies affecting @EnableMethodSecurity. Requires a running Spring application with method-level security annotations on generic type hierarchies. Liquibase is a CLI tool that does not use Spring Security, does not enable @EnableMethodSecurity, and does not start a Spring application context. The spring-core artifact is a transitive dependency.

vulnerabilities.description: In certain circumstances, Spring Boot's default web security is ineffective allowing unauthorized access to all endpoints. For an application to be vulnerable, it must be a servlet-based web application, have no Spring Security configuration of its own and rely on the default web security filter chain, depend on spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure, and not depend on spring-boot-health.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not include the actuator autoconfigure dependency required by this vulnerability.

analysis.detail: Spring Boot default web security bypass requires the application to depend on spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure and not depend on spring-boot-health. The repository's Spring Boot declarations are spring-boot-autoconfigure provided for Pro integration (pro/pom.xml:78) and spring-boot-starter-web in the license utility (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:44); grep for spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure, spring-boot-starter-actuator, and spring-boot-health across pom.xml files returned no matches.

vulnerabilities.description: A local attacker on the same host as the application may be able to take control of the directory used by ApplicationTemp. When server.servlet.session.persistent is set to true and the attack persists across application restarts, this may allow the attacker to read session information and hijack authenticated users or deploy a gadget chain and execute code as the application's user.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not configure persistent servlet sessions required to trigger this vulnerability.

analysis.detail: Spring Boot ApplicationTemp exploitation requires server.servlet.session.persistent=true and persistence across application restarts. Liquibase Secure's Docker image starts the Liquibase CLI entrypoint (docker/Dockerfile:68), and grep for server.servlet.session.persistent, ApplicationTemp, persistent=true, and setPersistent across Java, XML, properties, YAML, and YML files returned no matches.

Stack exhaustion DoS in json-smart via deeply nested JSON with many { characters (incomplete fix for CVE-2023-1370). Requires parsing attacker-controlled untrusted JSON input. Liquibase is a CLI tool that only processes JSON from local operator-controlled configuration files and database metadata. No network-facing JSON parsing surface exists.

Stack exhaustion DoS in json-smart via unlimited recursive parsing of deeply nested JSON arrays and objects. Requires parsing attacker-controlled untrusted JSON input. Liquibase is a CLI tool that only processes JSON from local operator-controlled configuration files and database metadata. No network-facing JSON parsing surface exists.

vulnerabilities.description: pgjdbc is an open source postgresql JDBC Driver. From version 42.2.0 to before version 42.7.11, pgjdbc is vulnerable to a client-side denial of service during SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication. A malicious server can instruct the driver to perform SCRAM authentication with a very large iteration count. With a large enough value, the client spends an unbounded amount of CPU time inside PBKDF2 before authentication can fail. A single attempt ties up a CPU core. Repeated or concurrent attempts exhaust client CPU and can wedge connection pools. In affected versions, loginTimeout did not fully mitigate this problem. When loginTimeout expired, the caller could stop waiting, but the worker thread performing the connection attempt could continue running and burning CPU inside the SCRAM PBKDF2 computation. This issue has been patched in version 42.7.11.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure distribution builds use PostgreSQL JDBC driver 42.7.11, which includes the fix.

analysis.detail: PostgreSQL JDBC SCRAM-SHA-256 client-side denial of service fixed in 42.7.11. Liquibase Secure distribution declares postgresql.version as 42.7.11 (dist/pom.xml:23) and uses that property for the org.postgresql:postgresql dependency (dist/pom.xml:115, dist/pom.xml:117), so the vulnerable 42.7.9 code reported by the scanner is not present in the current distribution build.

vulnerabilities.description:
Covert timing channel vulnerability in Legion of the Bouncy Castle Inc. BC-JAVA core on all (core modules). This vulnerability is associated with program files FrodoEngine.Java.
This issue affects BC-JAVA: from 1.71 before 1.84.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not use the affected Bouncy Castle Frodo post-quantum cryptography APIs.

analysis.detail: Bouncy Castle BC-JAVA FrodoEngine covert timing channel affects versions 1.71 before 1.84. Liquibase Secure distribution includes org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.78.1 (core/liquibase-dist/src/main/archive/licenses/commercial/README.txt:1318), but grep for FrodoEngine, Frodo, org.bouncycastle.pqc, pqc.crypto.frodo, and BCPQC across Java sources returned no matches, so the vulnerable Frodo post-quantum cryptography code path is not reachable.

vulnerabilities.description:
Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm vulnerability in Legion of the Bouncy Castle Inc. BC-JAVA bcprov on all (core modules).
This vulnerability is associated with program files G3413CTRBlockCipher.
This issue affects BC-JAVA: from 1.59 before 1.80.2, from 1.81 before 1.81.1, from 1.82 before 1.84.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not use the affected Bouncy Castle GOST 28147 CTR mode cipher APIs.

ratings.justification: Liquibase Secure does not call the Bouncy Castle GOST 28147 CTR mode cipher classes or related GOST APIs required to reach this keystream reuse vulnerability, so the vulnerable path is not reachable from application code.

analysis.detail: Bouncy Castle BC-JAVA GOST 28147 CTR mode keystream reuse affects bcprov-jdk18on versions from 1.59 before 1.80.2, from 1.81 before 1.81.1, and from 1.82 before 1.84. Liquibase Secure distribution includes org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.78.1 (core/liquibase-dist/src/main/archive/licenses/commercial/README.txt:1298), which is in the affected range. However, the vulnerable code path is not reachable from Liquibase code: focused greps across Java sources for G3413CTRBlockCipher, GOST28147, GOST, G3413, CTRBlockCipher, GOST28147Engine, and GOST28147ParameterSpec returned zero hits.

vulnerabilities.description: XML External Entity (XXE) via Unsanitized Dictionary Parsing in Apache OpenNLP DictionaryEntryPersistor. Versions before 2.5.9 and before 3.0.0-M3 initialize dictionary XML parsing without secure processing or DTD restrictions, allowing attacker-supplied dictionary files to trigger local file disclosure or server-side request forgery during SAX parsing.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure. The vulnerable OpenNLP dictionary parsing API is not reachable from production code.

analysis.detail: OpenNLP DictionaryEntryPersistor XXE vulnerability fixed in 2.5.9. Liquibase Secure declares opennlp-tools through opennlp.version 2.5.8 (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/pom.xml:76) in the phileas AI services dependency (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:18, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:19, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:20), but the vulnerable dictionary XML parsing API is not imported or called. The only production OpenNLP usage found is document categorization and tokenization (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/src/main/java/ai/philterd/phileas/service/ai/sentiment/OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java:22, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/src/main/java/ai/philterd/phileas/service/ai/sentiment/OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java:23, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/src/main/java/ai/philterd/phileas/service/ai/sentiment/OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java:24).

vulnerabilities.description: Apache OpenNLP ExtensionLoader is vulnerable to arbitrary class instantiation via attacker-controlled input passed to the extension loading mechanism, potentially allowing remote code execution.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure. The vulnerable OpenNLP ExtensionLoader API is not reachable from production code.

ratings.justification: Liquibase does not invoke the OpenNLP ExtensionLoader. Only pre-bundled document categorization and tokenization APIs are used.

analysis.detail: Apache OpenNLP ExtensionLoader arbitrary class instantiation vulnerability. The ExtensionLoader API is not imported or called anywhere in Liquibase Secure. The only production OpenNLP usage is document categorization and tokenization via DoccatModel, DocumentCategorizerME, and WhitespaceTokenizer in OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java; no extension loading or dynamic class instantiation occurs.
